title: Capacity Assurance: service-level spec and degradation notice protocol
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Define a compact, measurable SLA and associated error-budget/credit computation for Dedicated capacity customers that (a) ties to observable throughput and availability metrics, (b) integrates with autoscaling/fleet controls, and (c) specifies customer-facing notice and remediation language.

Scope: This ticket covers: the SLA objective definition (metrics, quantiles, aggregation windows), error budget math (how credits are computed and applied), a degradation corridor concept for phased remediation, autoscaling interactions (grace windows and burst entitlements), and contract/legal phrasing for notices, credits, and termination triggers. Non-goals: detailed billing invoice UX and backend billing integration (tracked in PM-155120).

Key proposals (summary):
1) SLA objective: "Committed Throughput" defined as a daily 95th-percentile of per-minute served throughput measured in tokens/second per GPU pool. Degradation threshold triggered when 24-hour rolling Committed Throughput falls below the committed rate for more than 30 continuous minutes.
2) Error budget: Measured as the percentage of minutes in a rolling 30-day window where Committed Throughput < committed rate. Credits are proportional: Credit% = min(100, (CommittedRate - ObservedRate)/CommittedRate * AllocationFactor) applied to the monthly reserved capacity fee. AllocationFactor defaults to 0.8 to reflect partial operator responsibility for transient congestion.
3) Degradation corridor: Introduce two remediation bands: "Notice Band" (5-15% below committed rate) with automated notification and accelerated autoscale; "Remediation Band" (>15% below) where credits accrue and manual escalation to ops is triggered.
4) Autoscale interplay: Customers may opt into an "Autoscale Assist" mode where Redwood will automatically provision burst capacity for short excursions. Burst capacity is limited to 2x baseline for up to 20 minutes per day without crediting. Longer bursts reduce the AllocationFactor for that day.
5) Fleet controls & failover: Committed Throughput is AZ-aware. If Redwood fails over customer traffic to a secondary AZ due to infrastructure outage, we consider served throughput equivalent for credit computation, but not if the customer requested failover.
6) Notice & remediation language: 72-hour window for formal notice before a contractual remediation or termination clause can be invoked; immediate temporary credits may be applied pending root cause analysis.

Measurement & instrumentation details:
- Primary metric: served_tokens_per_minute_per_pool (derived from token emissions and request counts).
- Aggregation: per-minute measurements, compute percentiles over 24h and 30d rolling windows.
- SLO alerting: fire at 10% error budget burn in 24h and at 50% in 7 days.
- Auditability: all raw minute-level data retained for 90 days accessible via console report and exportable CSV for contract disputes.

Credit computation worked example (illustrative):
- Committed rate: 1,000 tokens/s sustained (baseline).
- Observed 30-day rolling avg: 900 tokens/s -> shortfall 100 tokens/s -> shortfall fraction 10%.
- AllocationFactor: 0.8 -> Credit% = 10% * 0.8 = 8% -> Customer receives 8% credit on reserved capacity line item for the affected billing period.

Open questions for Legal/Finance:
- Cap on cumulative credits per year (proposed cap = 30% of annual reserved fee).
- Whether credits should be applied as invoice adjustments or as account credits in the Console.

Acceptance criteria:
- Draft SLA language ready for legal review and inclusion in Dedicated contract templates.
- Instrumentation and dashboard mock (console) showing committed throughput, error budget burn, and ledger of applied credits.
- Autoscale Assist config exposed in Console and documented in docs.

Deliverables:
- Contract paragraph (customer-facing) + internal playbook for ops.
- Data pipeline query and sample dashboard tiles.
- Runbook for customer notifications and escalations.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Luca Moreno: Initial write-up complete; flagged two measurement edge-cases: cold-start warming (first 10 minutes of a new pool) and KV cache priming. Asking SRE for instrumentation guidance.

2025-02-12 - Nadia Patel (Legal): High-level OK, need to limit ambiguous terms like 'sustained' and define whether token accounting includes retries. Also asked for cap on credits — proposing 25-35% band.

2025-02-12 - Owen Brooks (SRE): Suggested treating the first 15 minutes after a pool launch as 'warm-up' and exclude from rolling 24h windows. Recommended adding 'opportunity to remediate' clause of 60 minutes before applying credit when autoscale is in progress.
2025-02-13 - Maya Chen: Updated draft to add 'warm-up' exclusion and 60-minute remediation opportunity. Added AllocationFactor defaulting to 0.8 per Ops feedback. Sent for Legal quick review.
2025-02-14 - Legal review note (Nadia): Acceptable to proceed with 0.8 AllocationFactor and 30% annual cap recommended. Please add example contract clause for notice and cure periods.
decisions: Adopt 'Committed Throughput' measured as 95th-percentile per-minute throughput over 24h as the primary SLA signal.
Introduce a two-band degradation corridor (Notice Band and Remediation Band) with differentiated actions.
Default AllocationFactor set to 0.8; Finance to confirm cap on annual cumulative credits (proposed 30%).
notes: Ensure Console exposes both raw minute-level metrics and summarized SLO views. Autoscale Assist is opt-in and requires clear billing/credit implications in the UI.
